question.problem:
Find the solution $(a,b)$ to the following system of equations by eliminating the variable $a:$ 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5a+4b=7 \\ -2a+6b=20\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the $a$-coefficient in the first equation is $5,$ while in the second equation it is $-2.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $5,$ then the $a$-coefficient in the first and second equations will become $10$ and $-10,$ and these will cancel when we add the equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(\,5a+4b=7\,)\,\times (2) \\ (\,-2a+6b=20\,)\,\times (5)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}10a+8b=14 \\ -10a+30b=100\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $a$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{10a}+8b & =14 \\ -\cancel{10a}+30b & =100 \\ (8b+30b) & =(14+100) \\ 38b & =114 \\ b & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $b=3.$ However, we still need to find $a.$ To do this, we substitute $b=3$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5a+4b & =7 \\ 5a+4(3) & =7 \\ 5a+12 & =7 \\ 5a & =-5 \\ a & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-1$ and $b=3,$ which can be written as $(-1,3).$
